answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by rate-limiting identity creation and requiring proof of unique personhood for each new identity. Like a reef that grows slowly in a cold tundra ocean, each identity must pass a liveness check tied to one real person, and only a few may be created per period. An attacker wanting thousands of fake agents must therefore obtain thousands of distinct verified persons, which is slow, expensive, and easy to spot when many registrations cluster around one source. Legitimate agents pay almost nothing: one check, then they work freely.
